# Fin connection preview

ENG-13759 is an internal diagnostic experiment on `codex/fin-foreman-preview`. It uses the existing Foreman root and Eve channel runtime. Intercom restricts the connector to the `Foreman Preview - Aaron` audience: Type is User and Email is `aaron.fraga@acquisity.ai`. Customer workspace authorization is not implemented.

`POST /internal/fin-preview` requires a bearer token and is available only when `VERCEL_ENV=preview` and `FIN_FOREMAN_PREVIEW_ENABLED=true`. Set `FIN_FOREMAN_PREVIEW_TOKEN` only on this Preview branch. An empty body or empty inputs retain the synthetic connection test. A nonempty `question` starts a diagnostic task with read-only instructions and Deep Lake Software Workspace (owner `guy@deeplakesoftware.com`) supplied by the server for the approved case test. This prompt is an internal test fixture, not a tenant authorization boundary. Aaron remains the tester; references to "my workspace" target Deep Lake for this test. The investigation excludes prior Linear, Intercom, Slack and memory resolutions so the case can be compared independently. Restore the Aaron fixture before returning to ordinary Aaron-workspace tests.

The JSON response contains `status`, `message`, `probe` and `session_id`; diagnostics also return `run_handle`. `connected` proves only the synthetic reply. `completed` returns the diagnostic answer after the native task completes. `pending` means the result is not ready. Send the returned `run_handle` as `handle` to read that same run without starting another agent. The handle is signed with the existing Preview secret and checked before attaching to Eve's persisted event stream, so a caller cannot read an arbitrary Eve session by supplying its ID. Each new question starts a separate task; request retries are not deduplicated.

Set branch-scoped `FIN_FOREMAN_PREVIEW_SLACK_CHANNEL=C0BUF4GU8C8` for Aaron's `foreman-preview` channel, using `SLACK_CONNECTOR=slack/foreman-preview`. Starting a task posts a receipt and updates it with a readable status and the observed result. Probe and session IDs remain in the endpoint response rather than the Slack message. Diagnostics share a longer bounded result observer with Slack through Eve's `waitUntil`, while the HTTP response can return pending sooner. Result lookups do not post another receipt. Diagnostic answers are visible in Slack. Delivery is best effort; there is no outbox, retry worker, or guaranteed update after the observer expires or the hosting process fails.

When enabled, ordinary Executor calls on this Preview deployment select the dedicated `foreman-fin-preview` toolkit. Diagnostic provider reads use explicit operation allows and default deny. This experiment reuses the existing connections and helper bindings; it does not require new provider credentials. The existing support toolkit remains explicit, so both `FOREMAN_SUPPORT_ENABLED` and `FOREMAN_SUPPORT_FOLLOWUPS_ENABLED` must stay false. Toolkit policies restrict Executor operations, not browser, sandbox, GitHub, personal memory, all native agent tools, or customer rows. Existing authored Instantly helpers filter credential fields; raw operation grants do not provide that output filtering.

Live configuration verified 2026-09-12: 119 exact read approvals across 14 existing connection mounts. Coverage is PlanetScale (10), Sentry (6), Instantly (4), Autumn (28), Stripe (11), Inngest (18), Axiom (11), Intercom (11), Linear (16), Help Center (1), and Vercel diagnostics (3). There are no wildcard approvals; the final policy blocks all other operations. Sentry's unrestricted nested dispatcher is excluded. Axiom's existing OAuth authorization was reported expired and needs a successful live call before it can be counted as working. The ordinary Foreman and scheduled support toolkit records were verified unchanged.

Intercom's start connector `532961` uses this branch's Preview URL, its bearer token and the approved Vercel protection bypass. It sends fixed `action: "start"` with the Fin-collected `question`, then maps returned `run_handle` into the conversation attribute `Foreman Preview Run Handle`. Result connector `532990` sends fixed `action: "result"` and reads `handle` directly from that conversation attribute. Fin does not collect or copy the handle. Explicit starts require a question and ignore stale handles; explicit result checks require a handle and cannot fall back to starting a synthetic probe. The result connector remains directly available to the Aaron audience.

Procedure `2124573`, `Foreman Investigation — Aaron Preview`, is scoped to `Foreman Preview - Aaron` on Web. It calls the start connector once, supplies its generated `foreman_report` callback URL directly as `callback_url`, then waits for that webhook before displaying its `status` and `message`. Start connector direct triggering is disabled so the Procedure owns this sequence. It inherits communication style only, with escalation handled by its own start-failure and timeout instructions; Fin's built-in escalation still applies. An immediate start failure ends the Procedure; a missing callback times out after ten minutes and assigns the test to Aaron. Preview webhook values are samples and do not establish actual callback delivery; use Aaron's live Messenger for the full return-path test. Existing production workflows and abandoned diagnostic connectors are unchanged.

Procedure Step 2 must contain actual `@Read attribute` chips selected from Intercom's picker for `Webhook.foreman_report.message` and `Webhook.foreman_report.status`. Typing those names as plain text does not supply the callback values. Missing values must produce a report-retrieval failure, never an invented diagnostic answer.

Presentation changes on 2026-09-13 retain the existing communication-style guidance, including concise plain-language replies, no source sections unless requested, and the existing restriction on exact dollar amounts. The Aaron-only Procedure acknowledges the check as Fin, then summarizes the actual webhook evidence without naming Foreman or an internal handoff. It must preserve confirmed facts, material uncertainty and account-versus-workspace scope in both replies and handover summaries. Natural investigation requests no longer need to name Foreman. Foreman's handoff prompt asks for short paragraphs or bullets, normally under 200 words, with a brief source sentence and material limitations rather than an audit inventory. These are presentation instructions, not a new diagnostic-accuracy or customer-authorization guarantee.

The result connector uses the same customer presentation rules for manual retrieval. Its saved-reference mapping, direct triggering, and Aaron-only audience remain unchanged. Start connector direct triggering stays off. The Procedure skips its acknowledgement if Fin already sent one. The trigger explicitly distinguishes requests to inspect actual campaign names/data from general how-to questions, after a first natural campaign-name request in conversation `215475916985579` incorrectly received an article answer instead of starting a run.

Presentation validation on runtime commit `72f9daf`, Preview deployment `dpl_F9oEuTQe3vVcBPSqtbJSgirHu4qm`: `pnpm validate` passed all 766 tests, build passed, and the built GitHub proof passed all 31 callbacks. The first full validation attempt without `.env.example` lacked the local connector placeholders; the next hit a transient generated-module parse error in the capability tests. The unchanged capability tests and complete validation subsequently passed. No workaround or unrelated code change was added.

Live conversation `215475916990248` used the natural request "Can you check which campaigns are in my current workspace? Just the names, please." Session `wrun_41M2D9BGC00GTJK58GKY6BSJJ7` completed in 57 seconds with callback delivery logged. Fin automatically returned only the three campaign names, matching the readable [Preview Slack result](https://acquisityworkspace.slack.com/archives/C0BUF4GU8C8/p1789299901954599), without naming Foreman. A follow-up asking whether that meant all campaigns were sending correctly distinguished names from status. Manual result retrieval then used connector `532990` successfully (Intercom log `1271980271`), preserved that caveat, and started no new investigation. The first successful run sent two acknowledgements, motivating the conditional acknowledgement above.

The final fresh [conversation `215475917004291`](https://app.intercom.com/a/inbox/ls8uffkp/inbox/conversation/215475917004291) asked "Please check my current workspace and list the campaign names." Fin sent one acknowledgement, then automatically returned the three names with no Foreman reference. Session `wrun_41M2D9JB150GJEEYH13BN5HGBE` completed in 31.8 seconds; the [Slack result](https://acquisityworkspace.slack.com/archives/C0BUF4GU8C8/p1789300124838459) matched and explicitly limited its findings to names, not sending status. These two successful requests establish the observed presentation behavior only. Broader release UAT, long runs, customer isolation and diagnostic correctness remain separate acceptance work.

Escalation guideline `352613`, `Escalate unresolved technical issues for investigation`, overrode the Procedure for internal-domain users. Only this guideline now uses the new audience `Internal Test - except Foreman Aaron`: all original contact types, Email ends with `@acquisity.ai`, AND Email is not `aaron.fraga@acquisity.ai`. The shared `Internal Test` audience and live production workflow remain unchanged.

Callback starts return an acknowledgement as soon as Eve accepts the task. The Fin channel persists the callback URL and bounded latest final answer in native channel state, then posts from the task's completion or failure event. This survives the route's 120-second observation window without keeping an HTTP request open. The destination is restricted to the verified Intercom callback path, and its secret URL is omitted from the prompt and HTTP response. Delivery is best effort with a bounded request and no retry worker; manual signed result retrieval remains available if a callback fails.

The existing Foreman Preview Slack connector targets this branch at `/eve/v1/slack`; Production routing remains unchanged. Three live Messenger connection tests passed on commit `62b7b7f`, including a repeat and a new conversation, with matching completed Eve runs and Slack receipts. That evidence covers the synthetic connection only. Broader Slack UAT and customer isolation remain unproven.

The first live diagnostic on `9aa6dd2` completed in session `wrun_41M2BV5P2C0GYPFTXXRXQM0P82`, with production database, Autumn, Stripe and Instantly reads and its report posted to Slack. The same-conversation update request failed to retrieve it: Fin omitted the optional handle and started an empty synthetic probe instead. That demonstrated failure motivated the fixed start/result actions and conversation attribute mapping. The report also misinterpreted separate balance components as disagreement; current Acquisity code adds the Autumn and internal wallet balances. Tool access is proven for those observed reads, not diagnostic interpretation accuracy.

The first live Procedure run, `wrun_41M2BYVSX40GX5DSWNH5X1XTQ5` in conversation `215475914077959`, proved automatic callback delivery in approximately 80.6 seconds. Answer fidelity failed: Foreman reported campaign states `paused`, `draft`, `draft`, while Fin invented that all were sending. After publishing the actual `@Read attribute` chips, session `wrun_41M2BZ4YF00GN0367V73HTSJ57` completed in 40.7 seconds and automatically returned its report in live conversation `215475914092524`. Fin preserved the campaign table, evidence and caveats from the Foreman report without a follow-up message. This verifies callback transport and report fidelity for that run, not diagnostic accuracy: Foreman mislabeled Instantly status 2 as Active (the provider schema defines 2 as Paused, 1 as Active and 0 as Draft) and asserted complete pagination despite a continuation cursor. Those interpretation errors remain outside the connection experiment. See the [official campaign schema](https://developer.instantly.ai/api-reference/schemas/campaign) and [list endpoint](https://developer.instantly.ai/api-reference/campaign/list-campaign).

An artificial request to return a fixed test marker in conversation `215475914098155` was rejected by Fin's built-in safety guard (`OFFTOPIC_ABUSE`) before the Procedure or any connector ran. The experiment does not bypass Fin guardrails or guarantee triggering for arbitrary phrasing.

A second natural request, listing workspace campaign names, completed in session `wrun_41M2BZ9S6X0GPVY06AAB77N642` and conversation `215475914101039`. The start succeeded at 23:30:04 UTC; the callback resumed Fin at 23:31:05 and the report appeared at 23:31:06 without another user message. Its three names, workspace provenance, empty follow-up page and source-status caveats matched the Slack report. These two corrected runs prove observed automatic returns, not broad triggering reliability. The second Procedure's internal handover inaccurately called the campaigns active despite the displayed report only listing names; follow-up context fidelity remains unproven.
